claims.text: Low-concentration Co incorporation into SiO2-supported Ni nanoparticles shifts the Ni d-band center.
A shift in the Ni d-band center modifies the adsorption energies of key hydrogenation intermediates.
The modified adsorption energies enhance selectivity toward the desired hydrogenation product.
The electronic effect caused by Co incorporation improves catalyst durability relative to monometallic Ni.
SiO2 is an inert support in the proposed Ni catalyst system.
Co alloying tunes the electronic structure of Ni active sites through a shift in the d-band center.
The Co-induced electronic alteration facilitates formation of the desired hydrogenation product.
The Co-induced electronic alteration reduces catalyst-deactivation pathways.
Matched Ni-Co alloy nanoparticles will exhibit higher target-product selectivity than matched monometallic Ni nanoparticles under identical hydrogenation conditions.
Matched Ni-Co alloy nanoparticles will exhibit better durability than matched monometallic Ni nanoparticles under identical hydrogenation conditions.

The proposed mechanism is expected to apply to low-level Co alloying in Ni-based catalysts under hydrogenation conditions of 100–150 °C with controlled hydrogen pressure and matched physical parameters.
High Co concentrations may introduce ensemble or segregation effects that invalidate the proposed electronic-effect mechanism.
Surface segregation and ensemble effects may influence the catalytic performance independently of a d-band-center shift.
XPS and EXAFS characterization can help assess electronic changes and identify possible surface segregation or other structural alternatives.
